title: Variance bound by noisy total influence
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space with $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)>0$. For every $\rho>0$, $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)\,\rho^{I(f)/\operatorname{Var}_P(f)}\le\sum_S |S|\rho^{|S|}\mathbb E_P f_S^2$, where the sum is over all coordinate sets $S$, $f_S$ is the $S$-component, and $I(f)$ is the total influence.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with variance $V>0$, and $\rho>0$. Writing $I=\sum_iI_i(f)$ and $f_S$ for the orthogonal components, $V\rho^{I/V}\le\sum_S|S|\rho^{|S|}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$.
